evidence_notes: Claim: technology/emotion-recognition software is valuable in the classroom, stated in sentence 1 and held; support is drawn from the source (the 44 facial muscles and 3-D model detail, two attributed quotes from 'Paragraph six'), plus the reasoned point that a teacher cannot always be present so faster students move on while strugglers get help. Org 4 (controlling idea early and held, opening orients and closing closes, but the facial-recognition, typing, nonverbal-communication and video paragraphs could swap places freely). Dev 4 (specific source detail and quotes, connection stated in places - 'It could be more beneficial than a teacher, because...' - but quotes sit alongside the writer's sentences and several claims stay general, so not specific-plus-explained throughout). Conv 3 (errors accumulate - becomeing, effectivly, benefital, 'resource is the classroom', than/then - and sentences like the lab/science-class one force a re-read to repair). Arg 4 (at least one reason genuinely reasoned - why absent teacher time makes the tool useful - but no opposing consideration answered and 'it depends on whether the kid uses it' is a bare aside, not a qualification).

Claim: driverless cars are a bad idea, announced in the first clause; support is four asserted objections - children running into the street, gas already wasted, affordability/class resentment, and the cars people already own - with a brief lifted quote ('fundamentally change the world'). Org 3 (controlling idea stated up front and parts relate, but there is no closing at all - the text simply stops mid-point - so rung 4 fails on the frame). Dev 2 (support is offered but general throughout - no named case, figure or realized example; the child-in-the-street and used-car points are gestures, and the gas concession is answered with 'lots'). Conv 2 (the wealth/affordability stretch obscures meaning to the point where I have to guess the intent rather than repair it - 'think of themselfs not to good enough becusae... other words better than others in there point of view'). Arg 4 (position committed and at least one reason actually reasoned - danger follows because the car may not detect a child crossing - but nothing beyond the prompt's own framing and the gas counterpoint is raised, not answered).

Claim only surfaces in the final paragraph - we should not be limited by danger in what we want to study - after four paragraphs of Venus facts; support is source material (800 degrees, 90x atmospheric pressure, corrosive sulfuric acid clouds, two attributed quotes) plus a lifted unquoted stretch on volcanoes, earthquakes and lightning strikes. Org 3 (a controlling idea exists but is weakly located - the opening is a run of unanswered 5-W questions and the position appears only at the end). Dev 3 (specific figures present and one connection stated - 'This goes to show... you probaly would pass out or either die' - but the borrowed material is patchwritten, source phrasing stitched in with little transformation, which caps the trait). Conv 2 (frequent run-ons and wrong words - planted/plants, exiciting, discorved - and 'Venus causes many things to corrupt without venus there would be many corruptions in the world' has to be guessed at, not repaired). Arg 3 (position clear and committed once it arrives, but the reasons are asserted - 'the world be so much better if we did what we wanted' - never shown, and the danger facts run against the stance without being reconciled).

Claim: you should join the Seagoing Cowboys program, announced in the opening and restated in the close; support is Luke Bomberger, the 44 nations forming UNRRA and the horses, young cows and mules shipped overseas, plus destinations New Orleans and Greece, and the postwar rebuilding work. Org 4 (thesis early and held, frame present, all three reasons on topic, but the three reasons are interchangeable - phone/new experiences, animals and rebuilding could swap with no loss). Dev 4 (named specifics from the source and connections stated - 'This is your oppertunity to visit beautiful places' - but reason one is entirely general and the explanations mostly restate the support). Conv 3 (spelling and apostrophe errors accumulate throughout - experiance, frist, dastroyed, oppertunity, dont, lowercase new orleans - sentences run to one short pattern, and the endangered-animals sentence needs a re-read). Arg 4 (one reason actually reasoned - you cannot know it is boring until you try, so trying is warranted - but no opposing view engaged and the conclusion is exactly what the prompt implies).

Claim: studying Venus is a worthy pursuit, stated in sentence 1 and affirmed at the end; support is three source facts lifted almost verbatim without quotation marks (corrosive sulfuric acid clouds, 800 degrees, 90x pressure), and the justification offered is circular - 'these facts support my claim because you can research cool stuff... and thats how it supports my claim'. Org 3 (controlling idea stated but the opening immediately drifts into why Venus is unreachable, the closing only stops - 'this concludes all the stuff in my essay' - so the frame is perfunctory and rung 4 fails). Dev 3 (one specific piece of support present, but it is listed rather than explained and the borrowed phrasing is patchwritten straight from the source, which caps the trait). Conv 2 (very limited vocabulary - 'stuff', 'cool stuff' - and structural breakdown; the opening 'because no human could not live in venus' obscures meaning enough that I have to guess the intent). Arg 3 (position clear and committed - 'Yes i think it is' - but the reasons are restatements of the position and the stated reasons actually undercut it; nothing is reasoned).

Claim: join the Seagoing Cowboys, stated in the opening hook and driven home in the close; support is first-person specifics - nine trips, volleyball, baseball and table tennis tournaments on return voyages, the Panama Canal, Venice with streets of water, nearly falling off the ship, mucking stalls. Org 4 (thesis early and held, opening orients and the closing lands a call to action, but the games paragraph and the sights paragraph could swap without loss). Dev 4 (specific realized detail and connections stated - 'These are sights some only wish on going... Thats why I'm here, to tell you to join' - but the games are listed rather than explained, so not most-explained-adding-something). Conv 3 (spelling errors accumulate - invigerating, beatifull, steets, vollyball, wassafe, to/too - and 'These are sights some only wish on going' needs repair on a re-read). Arg 4 (a reason reasoned and the risk concession briefly answered, but the answer is a bare assertion of the good feeling, and the conclusion is exactly what the prompt's framing implies).

Claim: facial-coding technology in classrooms is valuable because knowing students' emotions lets others respond appropriately; the opening previews three grounds (communicate better, know when something should change, show empathy) and the body works through five attributed quotes from the article, including the 'smiling politician' quote applied to a student who says 'I understand' but does not mean it. Org 4 (thesis early, preview honoured, every part on topic, but the three grounds are parallel supports that could swap, and the closing reproduces the opening almost word for word). Dev 4 (support is specific and each quote is followed by a stated connection, but the explanations lean on restating the quote before a generic classroom application, and the quotes sit alongside the writer's sentences as dropped-in blocks rather than inside them). Conv 4 (few errors - infromation, truely, helpl - and the odd approximate word such as 'complement those emotions'; long sentences occasionally lose their grip but nothing has to be repaired, and sentence shape is too uniform for rung 5). Arg 4 (one reason genuinely reasoned - concealed incomprehension becomes visible, so teaching can be adjusted - but no opposing consideration, no cost acknowledged, and the conclusion is the one the prompt's framing implies).

Claim: the Face on Mars is a natural landform, stated in the opening with a preview and reaffirmed in the conclusion; support is erosion and rock formation plus shadows cast given Viking 1's angle, the April 5 1998 Mars Global Surveyor image on the JPL site, and the 2001 high-pixel camera clear enough to show Egyptian-style pyramids or a small shack. Org 4 (thesis early and held, frame present, all parts relate, but the three numbered reasons are interchangeable). Dev 4 (specific dated source evidence and the connection stated for some of it - shadows explain the eyes because of the direction Viking 1 faced - but the second reason reports the source without saying what it shows, so not explained throughout). Conv 3 (missing spaces after every period, dropped words - 'Some people would there are lifeforms' - surfurs, wedsite, 'could've have seen'; errors accumulate and the third-reason sentence needs a re-read to repair). Arg 4 (reasoning shown and one objection genuinely answered - water does not entail life, since a planet can have clouds and water without lifeforms - but the counterargument paragraph presents the other side without rebutting it, and the conclusion is one the prompt's framing already implies).

Claim: driverless cars should not be on the road because residual technological risk cannot be engineered away, qualified at the outset ('a neat idea but only if all of the things that could go wrong have been evaluated'); support is worked hypotheticals - a malfunction sending the car off a cliff or into another car, with the liability question taken from the passage, and a pedestrian struck with no warning - plus the drunk-driving death toll as a comparison. Org 4 (position early and held, frame present, all parts relate, but paragraphs two and three both work the same 'people will get hurt' ground and could swap). Dev 4 (a realized example whose connection to the claim is stated - the cliff crash would be the manufacturer's fault because nothing the driver did could prevent it - but the drunk-driver and death-rate claims stay general assertions, so support is not specific throughout). Conv 4 (run-ons, comma splices, missing question marks, to/too and then/than, but the voice is fluent and nothing has to be repaired; error density and uneven control keep it off rung 5). Arg 5 (the governing principle is made explicit - 'we should be more concerned with what could go wrong than what is cool' - the safety-claim objection is answered rather than mentioned - 'It's not just safe because the manufacturers say that it's safe' - and the burden-of-proof conclusion goes past what the prompt's framing implies; rung 6 fails because the strongest objection, that automation replaces human error, is met by assertion).

Opens by handing back the prompt ('The Author support the idea that studying venus is a worthy pursuit despite the dangers') and then dumps Venus facts - density and size, 800 degrees, 90x pressure, oceans and life, valleys mountains and craters, silicon carbide electronics lasting three weeks - most of them unattributed near-verbatim source sentences, and closes with self-contradiction about whether life exists there. Org 2 (no controlling idea the reader does not have to assemble; the paragraph break falls mid-sentence and the parts follow each other with no recoverable relation, so rung 3 fails). Dev 2 (specific figures are present but the borrowed material stands in for the argument - the essay reports what the source says instead of arguing from it, and nothing is explained or connected to any position). Conv 1 (judging the writer's own sentences rather than the lifted ones: 'the planet is delete at de solar system... it was delate' and 'In planet Venus there not are life, people can live there' are unrecoverable; errors are pervasive and reading is a decoding exercise). Arg 2 (a position appears only as the prompt's own wording returned with no commitment added, and what follows are unconnected facts rather than reasons).
